classification.difficultyReason: Select and link several isosceles base-angle relations, exterior and supplementary angles, a right-isosceles45° relation and a straight-angle equation without intermediate prompts, then interpret a reflex angle and prove uniqueness. Long connected angle reasoning with taught tools, without a new theorem.

content.prompt: What pairs of whole number values can $\theta$ and $\alpha$ take in the diagram below? Explain the procedure you followed to obtain your answer.

spec.description: Connected chain of triangles between a baseline and an inclined line, with five double-ticked equal segments, two triple-ticked equal segments, a right-angle square, reflex theta and alpha. Coordinate names are internal and are not printed.
spec.mathematics: AB=BE=EC=CF=FG; CD=DG; angle CDG is 90 degrees. A,B,C,D are collinear and A,E,F,G are collinear. Internal segments BE, EC, CF and CG remain visible.
spec.answerVisibility: No auxiliary vertex names, derived angle values or solution construction appear.

answer.short:
$\theta=342^\circ$, $\alpha=72^\circ$. This is the only pair.

Follow the equal-base-angle deductions through the adjoining isosceles triangles.
answer.worked:
For this explanation, name the baseline points $A,B,C,D$ from left to right and the inclined-line points $A,E,F,G$ from left to right. Let the small angle at $A$ be $x$.

Since $AB=BE$, $\angle AEB=x$, so the exterior angle $\angle EBC=2x$. Since $BE=EC$, $\angle BCE=2x$. In triangle $AEC$, $\angle AEC=180^\circ-3x$, so $\angle CEF=3x$.

Since $EC=CF$, $\angle CFE=3x$. Therefore
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-6x.\end{align*}$$
Because $E,F,G$ are collinear, $\angle CFG=180^\circ-3x$. Since $CF=FG$, the other two angles of triangle $CFG$ are equal, giving $\angle FCG=\tfrac32x$.

Triangle $CDG$ is right-angled and has $CD=DG$, so $\angle GCD=45^\circ$. Angles above the straight line at $C$ now give
$$\begin{align*}2x+(180^\circ-6x)+\tfrac32x+45^\circ&=180^\circ\\225^\circ-\tfrac52x&=180^\circ\\\tfrac52x&=45^\circ\\x&=18^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-18^\circ\\\theta&=342^\circ\\\alpha&=180^\circ-6\times18^\circ\\\alpha&=72^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The deductions determine $x$ uniquely, so there is only one whole-number pair.
